transcript: I don't know if I would sell my soul for a baseball team, but I would sell my soul to see this musical. I'm so excited to be back in DC and seeing Damn Yankees tonight. I have not seen the show before. I know very little about it except for for baseball. Damn Yankees is a classic golden age musical. It opened on Broadway in 1955. It won seven Tonys, including Best Musical. And it feels like it hits every O G. Classic musical box. A man makes a deal with the devil to make his baseball team better. The original production is set in the 1950s, and Arena Stage has kept all of the heart from the original production. Has done a few updates. Now the show is set in the year 2000, and Joe, our die hard baseball fan, loves the Orioles. But the choice is still the same. The team and the fame, or the life he left behind and the woman he loves. Okay, we're at the intermission, and this is so fun. The choreography is amazing. There are so many insane baseball numbers where they're like, doing backflips. The cast is ridiculous. Just so happy. I really did not know anything about the show, and I'm. And this cast is absolutely stacked. Rob Buckler is a devilishly hilarious apple game. Annaleigh Ashford is magnetic as Lola. Who's got the pain was a highlight of the whole night. Also, Alicia Umphres plays reporter Gloria Thorpe. I lost it during Shoeless Joe. And of course, Jordan Danica, who you just cannot help but fall in love with. His voice is unreal, and you just root so hard for him to succeed. And I really just love the entire ensemble. The choreography is so fun and athletic. It feels old school musical theater, but still fresh. Damn Yankees is playing at Arena Stage until November 9th. If you're in the area, I highly recommend you check it out. It is the baseball musical you didn't know you needed.
